app.name: Defroster
app.title: Defroster - Report Sightings
app.description: Real-time location-based safety alerts for ICE, Army, and Police sightings in your area

onboarding.title: Know when ICE, the Army, or police are nearby.
onboarding.sub: Defroster lets neighbors quietly warn each other. One tap sends an anonymous alert to everyone within 5 miles — no name, no account, no trace.
onboarding.ctaNote: We use your location only to show alerts near you. It never leaves your device with your name attached.

ios.title: Add Defroster to your Home Screen
ios.required: Required on iOS — alerts and notifications only work once Defroster is saved to your Home Screen as a web app.
ios.location: Also turn on {locationServicesLink} for Safari Websites, then save this site to your {homeScreenLink}.

privacy: Location is only used to find nearby alerts
Your spot is blurred to the nearest block (~250 ft)
Reports leave the server after 1 day
No personal data is ever stored
You can turn off location anytime
onboarding.story1: In the early hours of October 2, a South Shore Drive apartment building in Chicago was torn apart by a federal raid. Agents stormed the five-story complex with helicopters, armored vehicles, and flash-bang grenades. Families were forced from their homes, zip-tied in the street — some unclothed — and left outside for hours.
onboarding.story2: Incidents like this show the urgent need for tools that protect and inform. Defroster is an anonymous, open-source app that lets anyone report Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) activity with a single tap — so communities can stay safe, informed, and connected while remaining fully anonymous.

mainApp.notifWhy: Get a heads-up when something is reported within 5 miles.
mainApp.emptySub: No sightings reported around you right now.
mainApp.rightsCardSub: What to do if ICE is at the door — plain and clear.

report.title: What did you see?
report.sub: Pick one. Your report is anonymous and the location is blurred to the block.
report.doneSub: Neighbors within 5 miles have been notified. Thank you for looking out.

guide.title: Know Your Rights
guide.sub: What to do when U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is at the door. Save this. Share it.

rights: You have the right to remain silent. Use it.
Do not speak without a lawyer present.
Never lie or show false documents. (ICE can lie to you; you cannot lie to them.)
Memorize your A-number, your lawyer's phone number, and a family contact.
arrested: If you can't afford one, ask for a public defender.
Do not speak to law enforcement without a lawyer.

warrants.intro: This is the single most important thing to know. ICE cannot enter your home without a warrant signed by a judge.

points: Signed by a judge, from a real court.
Says “Search and Seizure” and lists your name & address.
Issued by ICE itself — not a judge.
Says “Warrant for Arrest of Alien”, not search.
Signed by an immigration officer, not a judge.
Does not let them enter your home.

warrants.ask: Ask them to slip the warrant under the door or hold it to a window. If there's no judge's signature, you do not have to open the door.
warrants.imgCaption: Real examples: a judicial warrant (left) and a DHS arrest warrant (right). ICE cannot enter your home with only the DHS document.

school.intro: Contact your local board of education and teachers' union to:
points: Ask how you can help — for all parents, not only immigrant families.

police.warn: Many areas have 287(g) agreements that require local police to work with ICE. Calling local police may bring ICE involvement.
police.what: 287(g) are federal agreements forcing local police to enforce immigration law — active in 1,000+ agencies across nearly all states. Only six states have banned them: Washington, Oregon, California, Illinois, New Jersey, and Connecticut.

items: Attend school board, city council, and town hall meetings. Join local immigrant-rights groups.
Call your representatives regularly. Push for humane policy and due process.
Volunteer for phone banks, door-knocking, petitions. Donate to local rights groups.
Follow non-profit investigative media. Share good information with your community.
Bring friends to meetings and actions. Build community networks.
800+ houses of worship offer shelter. Note: they have no special legal protection from warrants.
These are local agreements. Ask your city council, mayor, and police chief to end them.

points: Find an immigration lawyer before an emergency.
Be fully honest about your status — attorney–client privilege protects you.
Most firms offer help in multiple languages.

guide.takeaway: Know your rights, get legal help, and engage locally. Change happens at the community level.

footer.privacy: No accounts · No tracking · Open source
footer.disclaimer: Defroster is a community tool for safety information. It is not legal advice.

immigrationGuide.heading: Immigration Rights & Protection Guide

stoppedByICE.heading: If Stopped by ICE
rights: You have the right to remain silent—use it
Do not speak without a lawyer present
Never lie or provide false documents (ICE can lie to you; you cannot lie to them)
Memorize: your A number, lawyer's phone number, family contact
warrants: **Judicial warrant** (signed by a judge) = you must comply
**ICE detainer** (ICE's own document) = not legally binding, you can refuse
ICE cannot enter your home without a judicial warrant
Ask to see the warrant. If they don't have one, you can turn them away
arrested: If you can't afford one, request a public defender
Do not speak to law enforcement without legal representation

localPolice.heading: Local Police & 287(g) Agreements
localPolice.warning: **Warning:** Many jurisdictions have 287(g) agreements requiring local police to work with ICE. Calling local police may result in ICE involvement.
localPolice.whatIs287g: **What is 287(g)?** Federal agreements forcing local police to enforce immigration law. Currently active in 1,000+ agencies across nearly all states. Only six states have banned them: Washington, Oregon, California, Illinois, New Jersey, and Connecticut.

Donate to local immigration rights groups
stayInformed: Follow non-profit investigative media (ProPublica, The Appeal)
organize: Bring friends to meetings and actions
sanctuary: 800+ houses of worship offer shelter and support

Contact one if you need immediate assistance
repeal287g: These are LOCAL agreements requiring LOCAL approval
Contact your city council, mayor, and police chief to demand repeal
Show up to city council meetings
Even without 287(g), advocate for immigrant protection ordinances

tips: Contact an immigration lawyer before an emergency

story.paragraph1: In the early hours of October 2, a South Shore Drive apartment building in Chicago was torn apart by a federal raid. Agents from Border Patrol, the FBI, and the ATF stormed the five-story complex with helicopters, armored vehicles, and flash-bang grenades. Families were forced from their homes, zip-tied in the street—some unclothed—and left outside for hours. By sunrise, all but 37 were released, but residents returned to apartments trashed and a community deeply shaken.
story.paragraph2: Incidents like this highlight the urgent need for tools that protect and inform. {appName} is an anonymous, {openSourceLink} app that lets users report Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) activity with just a tap on their screen. The platform never stores personal data, automatically deletes reports from the server after one day, and alerts communities within a five-mile radius. With Defroster, people can stay safe, informed, and connected—while remaining fully anonymous.
